# Lowes.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/lowes-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/lowes-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects data from Lowes.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Lowe's Product and Pricing Data in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-lowe)
- **Code:** [`lowes.py`](lowes.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Products](results/products.json) · [Search](results/search.json) · [Store locations](results/store_locations.json)

## What it scrapes

- Lowes product pages
- Lowes search pages
- Lowes store locations

## Functions

- `scrape_products(urls)` → `List[LowesProduct]`: scrape product data from lowes product pages
- `scrape_search(query, max_pages=3)` → `List[LowesSearchResult]`: scrape Lowe's search results
- `scrape_store_locations(zip_code, max_results=10)` → `List[LowesStoreLocation]`: scrape Lowe's store locations nearest to a zip code

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import lowes


async def main():
    search = await lowes.scrape_search(query="cordless drill", max_pages=2)
    store_locations = await lowes.scrape_store_locations(zip_code="28202")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`LowesProduct`**: `product_id`, `item_number?`, `model_id?`, `url`, `name?`, `brand?`, `price?`, `selling_price?`, `currency?`, `description?`, `specifications`, `images`, `store_number?`, `zip_code?`
- **`LowesSearchResult`**: `product_id`, `item_number?`, `model_id?`, `url?`, `name?`, `brand?`, `price?`, `currency?`, `image?`
- **`LowesStoreLocation`**: `store_number`, `name?`, `address?`, `city?`, `state?`, `zip_code?`, `phone?`, `distance?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`lowes.py`](lowes.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/lowes-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_store_locations_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
